answer: A stake-bonded registry makes each identity costly: to join, an agent locks a refundable deposit in a shared vault, and its reputation graph treats every identity as a vertex whose past work is publicly auditable. Creating thousands of fake vertices means locking a deposit for each one, so the attacker pays linearly while honest agents pay once and earn the bond back through useful work. Slashing the vault deposit on proven fraud turns cheap duplication into a losing trade, since onyx-hard proof of past honest work cannot be copied without redoing the work and posting fresh collateral.
